 Appearance :

For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Anuj Kumar, Sr. Advocate
 Ms.Sakshi Bhatnagar, Advocate
 Ms.Eashita Raj, Advocate
 Ms.Gimni Priya, Advocate
 For the Respondent/s : Mr.Nirmal Kumar Sinha, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Bibek Chaudhuri
 Oral Order

By filing the instant application, it is submitted by the learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioner that the petitioner was convicted for committing offence under Section 498A of the IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

He was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment of two years and fine of Rs. 2 thousand for committing offence under Section 498A of the IPC and simple imprisonment of six months with fine of Rs. 2 thousand for the offence under Section 4 of the D.P.
Act.
2. The order of conviction and sentence by the Trial Court was affirmed by the Court of Appeal.
3. After delivery of judgement by the Court of Appeal, Patna High Court CR.

REV. No.174 of 2025(4)
dt.05-05-2025 the petitioner surrendered before the learned SDJM, Gaya on 22nd of April, 2025.

After surrender, the petitioner has preferred the instant application praying for bail on the ground that challenging the order of conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court and affirmed by the Court of Appeal.
The petitioner has filed the instant criminal revision.
Now during the pendency of the revision, if the petitioner remains in custody to serve sentence, the revisional application will be infructuous.
4. The learned APP for the State has not raised any objection against the prayer for bail.

On the Md. Naushad Khan vs The State Of Bihar on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171741117/
1 other hand, it is submitted by him that in all fitness of the things, the petitioner ought to be released on bail pending disposal of the instant revision.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. I have duly considered the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties.
6. As the instant revision is pending for disposal, this Court is of the view that the petitioner cannot be obligated to serve sentence before disposal of the revision.

7. Considering such aspect of the matter, let the petitioner above-named be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with one sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of learned SDJM, Patna High Court CR.

REV. No.174 of 2025(4)
dt.05-05-2025 Gaya, in connection with Complaint Case No. 941 of 2008, Trial No. 431 of 2019,
until further order.
8. Therefore, the instant revision is admitted.

9. Issue notice to private opposite party by both modes i.e., under ordinary process as well as registered cover with A/D, on steps being taken by the petitioner for filing requisites etc., within a period of one week from the date of this order.
10. The instant revision be listed after service of notice.
11.
In the meantime, Lower Court Record be called for.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) uttam/-
